clue.text: A crumb brush

definitions.meaning: a crumb is a small leftover morsel or fragment
a brush is a minor skirmish or fight, as in a brush with the law

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a tiny fragment of food, and a short scuffle or fight between people.

clue.text: After the British game, getting drunk

indicators.note: the game is placed after the British abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: After playing a very British game, someone ends up tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for very drunk, used especially in Britain.

clue.text: Lit up, getting into a fight with a weapon

indicators.note: one piece gets inside the other, so these words signal a container

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk ('lit up') gets into a brawl armed with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' reads as slang for drunk, but 'up' is the reversal signal (this is a down clue) and 'getting into' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim dagger with a narrow blade is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Stops and picks up

definitions.meaning: to halt or check something, as in halts progress
police pick up a suspect when they take them into custody

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: it halts something, and it takes someone into police custody.

clue.text: Only does the outside, but it makes one feel better

indicators.note: the swindles word goes around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, and cons means swindles
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Someone does only the exterior of a job, but it still cheers them up.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone in distress is to make them feel better.

clue.text: Less dash

parts.note: a dash written in a sum that means less, the symbol for subtraction

explanation.definitionFit: The symbol for subtraction is a short horizontal dash, read as less.

clue.text: They can turn people into stone

definitions.text: They can turn people into stone

parts.words: They can turn people into stone
parts.note: reads like gorgons or witches petrifying victims, but means carvers making statues of people

explanation.surface: A mythical image of monsters that petrify their victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists who carve figures make images of people out of stone.

clue.text: Leave when it's good and hot outside

indicators.note: the word hot sits outside the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Advice to go when the weather is fine and hot outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang command meaning go away, clear off or leave.

clue.text: Notice upside-down saying "School"

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a note is a written notice or memo

explanation.surface: A sign hung upside-down announces the word School.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English public (private boarding) school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Sham sick in it to get medication

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, so in signals a container

parts.note: paste is imitation jewellery, a sham gem
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be ill in order to get some medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicated lozenge sucked to soothe a sore throat is a form of medication.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty chance the drunkard will go back to drink

indicators.note: the drunkard's word goes backwards in the answer

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
to sup is to drink, or a sup is a mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A drunk will always return to the bottle, it's an even bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation with an even chance either way, decided as if by flipping a coin.

clue.text: A kind and good person with a heart of gold

indicators.note: the second piece forms the centre of the first, so this signals a container

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a good person
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A kind and good-hearted person is described as having a heart of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A type or variety of thing, as in what kind of car.

clue.text: Eels swimming in barrels, lacking air

indicators.note: the jumbled piece goes inside the barrels, a container

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

indicators.note: eels swimming about suggests their letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eels swim about in barrels with no air to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking air' sounds breathless, but air here means a tune or melody, not oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Air means a melody, so something without one has no tune.

clue.text: Save money by getting a local job

definitions.note: the definition describes the person by what they do; the answer is the person who has that job

parts.note: save means except, and so does bar, as in all bar one
tender is money, as in legal tender

explanation.surface: Someone saves money by taking a job close to home.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and someone serving drinks there works behind its bar.

clue.text: The bean, perhaps, to go with a rich stew

indicators.note: letters cooked up in a stew are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bean that might go well with a hearty stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white variety of bean, the kind used in baked beans and stews.

clue.text: Chopped up is simmered, covered in water

indicators.note: chopping up a word breaks its letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: chopped vegetables simmered under water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunged in so that it is fully submerged beneath liquid.

clue.text: Give a reason why you shouldn't put your name to it

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
to sign is to put your name to a document

explanation.surface: Advice on why not to sign a document.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over or deliver something into another's keeping.

clue.text: Upset, left the act

parts.note: over means left, as in left over or remaining
a turn is an act on stage, as in a comedy turn

explanation.surface: A performer upset at walking out of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock over or reverse something, in the way a court overturns a verdict.

clue.text: Married, with a lover, gets thrown out-expulsion

indicators.note: being thrown out of shape suggests these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A married person with a lover is thrown out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of someone or something, taking it away.

clue.text: Stock reaction to fear

parts.note: reads like a standard response to fright, but stock means livestock, and this is cattle panicking

explanation.surface: A stock or standard response to being frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd of cattle or horses.

clue.text: Some red dye swirling round in the water

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some red dye swirls around in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small whirlpool or circular current in water.

clue.text: I had mentioned, or observed

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the contraction is heard rather than written

parts.note: contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: A remark that something had been mentioned or noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at or watch something closely.

clue.text: Is out of one's way, going backwards

parts.note: ex means out of or from
one is I, and one's is I's

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone is going out of their way by retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, to have existence.

clue.text: Alarm sounded for a pretty girl

indicators.note: the alarm is spoken, so the word is heard as another

parts.note: a bell is an alarm

explanation.surface: Someone raises the alarm on behalf of a pretty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautiful woman, especially the most admired at an event.

clue.text: Used one to take the underground?

definitions.text: Used one to take the underground?

parts.words: Used one to take the underground?
parts.note: used to means accustomed, so this describes someone hardened to riding the tube

explanation.surface: A question about a regular passenger on the underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed or hardened to something unpleasant, used to it.

clue.text: Got into bed a wreck

indicators.note: a wreck is something broken, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed into bed, an exhausted wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired or came to have something.

clue.text: Aim to raze

definitions.meaning: to aim a gun, point it straight at a target
to raze is to knock a building flat to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: pointing a weapon at a target, and flattening a building.

clue.text: It might give one a bang on the forehead

definitions.text: It might give one a bang on the forehead

parts.words: It might give one a bang on the forehead
parts.note: a bang suggests a blow, but bangs are a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: Something that might cause a knock on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo; bangs is the American word for a fringe cut across the brow.
